title: `gather_for_metrics` and `GradientState` don't work with arbitrary evaluation intervals
author: ernestchu

comments.author: ernestchu
comments.body: After some investigations, I know the `GradientState` is synced by the **singleton class** design. My current workaround is manually setting `accelerator.gradient_state.end_of_dataloader` to `False` after the evaluation, so the following training would not incorrectly drop samples.

comments.author: muellerzr
comments.body:
@ernestchu `GradientState` is a singleton designed to work with a single dataloader that is currently being iterated upon, which is why you're experiencing this trouble. One thing I could think of is setting an api such as `pause` and `resume` which will "turn off" `GradientState` and/or reset it. So essentially the API would be:

```python
dl1, dl2 = accelerator.prepare(dl1, dl2)
for i,batch in enumerate(dl1):
    ...
    if i == 5:
        accelerator.gradient_state.pause()
        for batch in dl2:
            ....
        accelerator.gradient_state.resume()
    ...
```

Does this seem reasonable to you both @ernestchu @sgugger

The other thought would be just explicitly switching dataloaders, e.g. `accelerator.gradient_state.switch(dl2)`

comments.author: muellerzr
comments.body: Should be closed with https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/pull/1162, doesn't require any modification in the code
